rule.source: corpus/SOURCES.md:16 (S003) at BASE: 'The description cannot contain XML tags'
rule.live_wording: platform.claude.com agent-skills best-practices, fetched 2026-10-21: YAML Frontmatter note, description: 'Cannot contain XML tags' (the name bullet carries the same words)
rule.scope: description value only; the name bullet is out of C2 scope and is not labelled here
rule.stricter_external_rule: anthropics/skills skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py (fetched 2026-10-21): 'Description cannot contain angle brackets (< or >)'. Not the S003 wording; used only as a candidate predicate (builtin:anthropic-quick-validate)

label_definition: tag = the description VALUE (the YAML-parsed string) contains a substring matching XML 1.0 5th ed. STag [40], ETag [42] or EmptyElemTag [44], with Name [5] over NameStartChar [4] and NameChar [4a], Attribute [41] with Eq [25] and AttValue [10]; not-tag = no such substring. Markdown code spans, entity encoding, comment and CDATA wrappers are not exemptions: consumers insert the value raw (see resolution).
ambiguity_policy: s003_ambiguous=true only where the S003 vocabulary ('XML tags': comment, doctype, PI, malformed tag-shaped text, XML edition) or an unexcluded consumer step (NFKC) leaves the label open. `label` is the strict-grammar reading and `alt_label` the other reading. Rows where S003 is silent but consumer evidence decides are decisive and carry `resolution`. The gate counts only s003_ambiguous=false rows.
subject: value (YAML-parsed). Rows whose source differs from the value (folds, escapes, comments) are labelled on the value. The BASE grep checks source text and is scored as a predicate, not as ground truth.
value_derivation: PyYAML 6.0.3 safe_load at generation; cross-checked with ruamel.yaml (YAML 1.2) and with the lane's structural parser in C2Battery.yamlcheck.json

description: >
  Prompt & skill craft — audits, writes, and rewrites SKILL.md / AGENTS.md /
  dispatch prompts / system prompts for trigger fidelity and decision density.
  Triggers: "skill file", "SKILL.md", "frontmatter description", "trigger
  words", "prompt craft", "write a skill", "audit this skill", "skill quality".
  Anti-triggers: general prompt engineering for model outputs (not skill
  files), runtime code changes, and domain content inside a skill's
  reference/ tree. Sibling boundary: the five `*-shokunin` domain skills
  (kagi, kake, kasegi, kengaku, kumitate) own their own SKILL.md content —
  this skill audits and reports; fixes route to the owning lane. Note: the
  shokunin files are not in an omp skill discovery root, so their descriptions
  never reach the `<skills>` router — craft here is audit-side, not
  router-visible.
